provenance: Pinned OSHB/WLC original source words and source-linked BDB/Strong dictionary cards; proposal is editorial and unapproved.

research_notes.text: Bara is a Qal wayyiqtol verb here. The OLT owner-lock is shaped, not created. English past follows the actual source form.
Tanninim is plurally aquatic-context creatures; traditional versions include sea monsters, dragons and great sea creatures. 'Great sea-creatures' remains a nonapproved English semantic proposal.
Nefesh has a wider source range than a modern immaterial 'soul'. 'Living soul' deliberately preserves the Hebrew noun/adjective distinction; its contextual sense remains under editorial review.
Shartzu is source-tagged Qal qatal 3cp; 'swarmed' does not derive from the wayyiqtol mandate here.
Vayvarekh is Piel wayyiqtol 3ms; English blessed is simple past.
Otam = direct-object marker plus 3mp pronominal suffix and receives them; bare et in the same verse has a zero standalone English gloss.
Peru is Qal imperative 2mp; Be fruitful is a command, never a wayyiqtol narrative past.
Urvu is imperative 2mp, but following yirev is jussive 3ms; both may have command force while their morphology differs.
Lemīnah here has a third feminine-singular suffix, expressed in OLT as her kind. This is a grammatical convention, not a repeated Bible-wide gender disclaimer.
Asah, here a wayyiqtol, must render He made, never shaped; the different Hebrew verb bara used in Gen 1:21 remains shaped.

A Christian canonical reader can compare divine agency in Genesis 1 with John 1:3. This is interpretive theological cross-reference, not proof that Hebrew bara lexically denotes Christ or shares a Greek homonym.

verse_research.english_main_research_proposal: And God — He shaped the great sea-creatures, and every living soul creeping, which the waters swarmed to their kinds, and every bird of wing to his kind; and God — He saw that — good.
And God — He blessed them, saying: Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the Seas; and the bird — let [he] multiply in the Earth.
And was evening, and was morning: day fifth.
And God — He said: Let the Earth bring forth living soul to her kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of Earth to her kind; and so was.
And God — He made the beast of the Earth to her kind, and the cattle to her kind, and every creeping thing of the ground to his kind; and God — He saw that — good.
